drhp.business: Manipal operates a pan-India network of multispecialty hospitals delivering care from outpatient services to complex tertiary and quaternary interventions. As of September 30, 2025 it ran 38 hospitals (48 on a pro forma basis) with 10,761 licensed beds (12,367 pro forma) across 14 states and union territories. Clinical focus is on tertiary/quaternary care in cardiac sciences, oncology, neurosciences, gastro sciences, orthopedics and renal sciences (CONGO-R).

drhp.end_markets: Insurance / Third party administrators (~49.18% of revenue, FY2025 restated)|Cash / self-pay (~31.20% of revenue, FY2025 restated)|Government (~13.41% of revenue, FY2025 restated)|Others (~6.21% of revenue, FY2025 restated)
drhp.expansion: Manipal plans to add approximately 751 licensed beds across existing hospitals and approximately 1,943 licensed beds through greenfield projects by 2030 to support growth. Its network grew from 28 hospitals with 7,699 licensed beds (Mar 31, 2023) to 48 hospitals with 12,367 licensed beds (pro forma, Sep 30, 2025), aided by acquisitions of AMRI (Sep 2023), Medica Synergie (Jul 2024) and Sahyadri (Oct 2025, adding 1,606 beds). In November 2025 it commenced its 49th hospital in Bengaluru, taking licensed capacity to 12,631 beds as of December 31, 2025.
drhp.mdna: Inpatient volume growth (0.28m in FY2023 to 0.44m in FY2025, 25.72% CAGR) driving revenue|Rising CONGO-R high-acuity specialty mix supporting ARPOB and revenue quality|Operational efficiency - ALOS held at 2.85-2.88 days (FY2023-FY2025), declining to 2.73 days in H1 FY2026|Occupancy and operational-bed ramp of acquired/upgraded hospitals|Post-acquisition margin improvement (e.g. Columbia Asia EBITDA margin 27.41% to 31.95%)|Material cost to revenue held stable around ~20%

business_ops.seasonality: No quantified seasonality is disclosed. The Risk Factors note that patient volumes and hospital occupancy are affected by factors including febrile illness cycles, climate and weather conditions, patient demand and competition.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Not a manufacturing supply chain. The DRHP describes an integrated, decentralized multi-hospital operating model (regional COOs, hospital directors and medical directors) and a vertically integrated clinical-talent pipeline: a DNB/DrNB/FNB ecosystem spanning 343 seats across 25 hospitals, 42 specialties and 659 students enrolled as of September 30, 2025 (pro forma), plus collaboration with Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE) which supports doctor recruitment. Growth is driven by organic brownfield/greenfield expansion and strategic acquisitions (AMRI – September 2023, Medica Synergie – July 2024, Sahyadri – October 2025).

concerns_observed: Sharp leverage step-up: total borrowings jumped to Rs 10,111.10 cr at H1 FY26 (from Rs 4,766.83 cr FY25), driven by a Rs 5,310 cr NCD issuance by material subsidiary MHPL (9.03%) to fund the Sahyadri acquisition; aggregate borrowings Rs 10,612.78 cr at Jan 31, 2026 with 43.61% at variable rates - partly cushioned by Rs 5,446.18 cr cash at H1 FY26.

Acquisition-led model and pro forma reliance: much of the network scale (48 hospitals pro forma vs 38 actual) rests on recent M&A; the pro forma financials are illustrative only, and SHPL's H1 FY26 interim statements carry a qualified audit opinion.
Persistent Karnataka concentration: even after diversification, ~half of revenue (49.55% H1 FY26) still comes from a single state.

High and rising related-party intensity: recurring brand royalty/back-office charges to MEMG (Rs 35.61 cr FY25), management fees to Manipal Academy of Higher Education (Rs 39.02 cr FY25), plus large inter-corporate deposit and expense-recovery flows with group entities.

Cost structure exposure: doctors' professional fees (21.82% of revenue H1 FY26) plus employee benefits (14.57%) leave margins sensitive to talent costs and the new Labour Codes (effective Nov 21, 2025).

Payor and pricing risk: insurance/TPA (50.37%) plus government schemes (13.42%) are ~64% of gross inpatient revenue, exposing the Company to collection delays, DPCO price caps and EWS/free-bed obligations (Supreme Court EWS summons dated March 9, 2026).

Litigation and contingent overhang: outstanding proceedings aggregate ~Rs 294.09 cr against the Company and ~Rs 426.43 cr against subsidiaries; contingent liabilities Rs 183.86 cr plus an RSDH (Malaysia) performance indemnity of ~Rs 780.12 cr.
The Company receives no proceeds from the Rs-value Offer for Sale (up to 43,227,668 shares by promoter/investor sellers).

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue CAGR 30.50% and PAT CAGR 61.60% FY23-FY25; largest network by beds (12,631 licensed by Dec 31, 2025) and 2nd by hospital count; expansion pipeline ~751 brownfield + ~1,943 greenfield beds by 2030.
RoNW improving to 18.16% and RoCE 26.98% (FY25); occupancy 65-67%; but H1 FY26 RoNW annualises off an enlarged, cash-heavy equity base (Rs 6,419.44 cr net worth).
CFO positive and above PAT every year (Rs 1,569.83 cr vs Rs 1,081.67 cr in FY25); FY25 investing outflow Rs 2,658.34 cr reflects acquisition/PPE spend.
Total debt Rs 10,111.10 cr at H1 FY26 after the Rs 5,310 cr MHPL NCD; offset by Rs 5,446.18 cr cash and a Rs 5,378 cr Fresh-Issue NCD repayment, but 43.61% of debt is variable-rate.
Annuity-like hospital demand and diversified specialties, but ~49.55% single-state (Karnataka) concentration and ~64% insurance/TPA + government payor mix with collection/pricing risk.

Heavy RPTs (MEMG royalty, MAHE fees), Temasek + MGHS joint control under a Restated Inter-se Agreement, a USD 600M charge over promoter MGHS shares, DBS repayment conflict, untraceable historical records, and a board where all three independents were appointed only on Feb 18, 2026 after six director exits in FY26.

Fresh Issue up to Rs 8,000 cr benefits the Company (NCD repayment + SHPL buyout); a Pre-IPO Placement up to Rs 1,600 cr may cut the Fresh Issue; price band, total offer size and P/E are shown as [.] so valuation is undetermined against FY25 EPS Rs 9.25 (H1 FY26 EPS Rs 4.86).

red_flags: Charge over promoter shares: MEMG International Ltd created a fixed and floating charge over its shareholding in promoter Manipal Global Health Services for a USD 600M KKR facility (agreement dated May 20, 2025); enforcement could change control of a key promoter.
Conflicted use of Net Proceeds: Rs 5,378 cr repays MHPL NCDs held by DBS Bank Ltd, whose Indian subsidiary is a BRLM to the Offer and a deemed 'associate' of Selling Shareholder Imperius.

Brand monetisation with the promoter group: allotment of 23,820,811 shares to MEMG at Rs 692.68 for consideration other than cash (March 12, 2026) to settle the Restated Brand License Agreement, on top of recurring royalty charges to MEMG.
Bonus issue 2:1 on April 22, 2025 falls within the regulatory 18-month window before the DRHP - a lock-in/eligibility flag, not merely elapsed time.
Untraceable corporate records: certain letters of renunciation, share transfer forms/DIS slips and demat statements are not traceable.

Reputational/criminal exposure: FIR dated April 17, 2024 over an alleged kidney-transplant racket at Manipal Hospital Jaipur, ED summons to a hospital director, and an organ-transplant licence suspension.
Data and cyber incidents: an October 24, 2024 data breach compromised ~1,200-1,500 doctors/patients (DPDP penalties up to Rs 250 cr), plus a CCTV ransomware incident at Vijayawada.
Board instability: six directors exited between June 2025 and March 2026 and all three independent directors were appointed only on February 18, 2026, so independent oversight is newly constituted.
Pro forma financials are illustrative only and SHPL's H1 FY26 interim statements carry a qualified audit opinion.
Promoters' average acquisition cost is well below the likely Offer Price (e.g. Imperius Rs 68.73, Dr. Ranjan Ramdas Pai Rs 44.53, MEMG India Rs 102.56 per Rs 2 share).
strengths_observed: Scale leadership: India's largest multispecialty hospital network by bed capacity (10,761 licensed beds actual / 12,367 pro forma as of Sept 30, 2025; 12,631 by Dec 31, 2025) and the second largest chain by number of hospitals; the only private chain with leadership in three metros (Bengaluru, Kolkata, Pune) per the CRISIL Report.

Industry-leading growth: revenue from operations compounded 30.50% (Rs 4,839.61 cr FY23 to Rs 8,242.25 cr FY25) and profit for the year 61.60% (Rs 414.20 cr FY23 to Rs 1,081.67 cr FY25); H1 FY26 revenue Rs 4,713.05 cr and PAT Rs 571.83 cr.
Profitable with improving returns: RoNW rose 12.70% (FY23) to 14.75% (FY24) to 18.16% (FY25); RoCE 27.74% FY24 and 26.98% FY25; operational-bed occupancy steady at 63.47% to 67.09% across the period.
High-quality earnings: operating cash flow was positive and exceeded PAT every year (CFO Rs 1,152.06 cr FY23, Rs 1,388.65 cr FY24, Rs 1,569.83 cr FY25; Rs 942.09 cr H1 FY26).

Reducing geographic dependence: Karnataka fell from 66.61% of revenue (FY23) to 51.55% (FY25) to 49.55% (H1 FY26) as eastern India scaled from 2.33% to 23.81%, diversifying the base while retaining a high-acuity CONGO-R specialty mix (~60-64% of gross inpatient revenue).

Fresh Issue is deleveraging/strategic: of the up-to Rs 8,000 cr Fresh Issue, Rs 5,378 cr repays MHPL NCDs and Rs 574 cr buys out Sahyadri (SHPL) minority - both accrue to the Company (OFS proceeds do not).

Marquee institutional backing and management: Temasek-affiliated promoters (Kangto, Kabru, Imperius) and TPG, an experienced MD & CEO (Dilip Jose), and a repeatable acquisition-integration playbook (Columbia Asia, AMRI, Medica Synergie, Sahyadri).
Accreditation and brand: 41 of 48 hospitals NABH-accredited, 25 labs NABL-accredited; flagship Old Airport Road hospital rated No.1 in Bengaluru for 20 years.
